name: ZAG
zag_role: Slovenian National Building and Civil Engineering Institute
description: Founded 1994. 255 staff, six research and testing departments, a metrology department and three notified-body services under the Construction Products Regulation. Home of SiWIM bridge weigh-in-motion and of the BrAId project applying machine learning to B-WIM data quality.
history: The institute traces its origin to 18 July 1949, when the first building and civil engineering institute in Slovenia was set up with twelve staff. It was renamed the Institute for Testing and Research in Materials and Structures, ZRMK Ljubljana, in 1952, by which time it had grown to 150 employees and had its own building on Dimičeva. After independence the government reorganised ZRMK in 1994 and 1995 and split it into two bodies. ZAG was registered on 17 March 1995 and began operating on 1 April 1995 as a governmental non profit research institute, a status that lets it act as an independent third party in testing and certification. It is organised into five departments, Materials, Building Physics, Fire Safe Sustainable Built Environment, Structures, and Geotechnics and Infrastructure, together with the Laboratory for Metrology, the Certification Service and the Service for Technical Assessment and Approvals.

source_differences: Floors of the 1984 office building: 7 floors (dLib source, "A seven-storey facility"), and ZAG staff confirm 7 floors, at least on the left side of the building (stated 12 November 2026, the other side was not counted). The GURS cadastre gives 8 storeys for building 892, a count that includes storeys below ground. An earlier count of 6 on photographs is withdrawn.

Height of the office building (cadastre building 892): the cadastre gives 23.5 m for the highest point above the terrain. Inside the same outline the laser scan surface has its middle at 21.9 m, 99 % of it stays below 26.3 m, and the highest pixel is at 27.0 m. The sources do not say what stands above 23.5 m. Laser scanning of Slovenia (GURS, CLSS, file series NDMP), read 12 November 2026.

Height of cadastre building 8300: the cadastre gives 10.0 m for the highest point above the terrain, while 99 % of the laser scan surface inside the outline stays below 13.2 m and its middle is at 9.0 m. Laser scanning of Slovenia (GURS, CLSS, file series NDMP), read 12 November 2026.

Figures in the record text: 255 staff against 254 at the end of 2023 in the ZAG book of 2024, six departments in the description against five in the history text, and 1952 against 1953 for the renaming to ZRMK within the same book.

Extent of the site: the GURS cadastre lists ZAG as manager of 14 buildings and 23 parcels in Bežigrad. ZAG staff state that the south-west corner towards Ptujska ulica is not part of ZAG. So the small buildings 1321 and 1365 and six parcels (258/1, 258/6, 258/7, 259/1, 259/2, 246/4) are not drawn. The long building 1079 is drawn. The cadastre and the owner are not reconciled on that corner.
